clues: The world's largest particle accelerator runs through a 27 km circular tunnel about 100 metres underground, on the border between two countries.
The laboratory was established in 1954 in a western suburb of a city on the France–Switzerland border, and the World Wide Web was invented there in 1989.

reveal.explanation: CERN is based in Meyrin, a western suburb of Geneva, on the France–Switzerland border. Established in 1954, it runs the Large Hadron Collider in a 27 km tunnel about 100 metres underground; the World Wide Web was invented there by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.

sources.excerpt: CERN, established in 1954, is based in Meyrin, a western suburb of Geneva, on the France–Switzerland border (46.2330°N 6.0556°E). The LHC uses the 27 km circumference circular tunnel, located 100 metres underground. In 1989, the World Wide Web was invented at CERN by Tim Berners-Lee.
